articles.title: Budget Traveller | 10 Border Villages To Explore In India Under Rs 35,000 From Delhi
articles.description:
India’s border villages offer travellers a glimpse of a side of the country that is rarely seen on conventional tourist itineraries. Far from crowded cities and commercial holiday destinations, these settlements combine dramatic landscapes, local traditions, fascinating history and stories of resilience. Prime Minister Narendra Modi has also highlighted the importance of developing border villages through initiatives such as the Vibrant Villages Programme. Better roads, connectivity and tourism infrastructure are gradually making several of these remote destinations more accessible. From Arunachal Pradesh and Ladakh to Punjab and Gujarat, these villages offer very different experiences. For travellers looking to explore India beyond the usual tourist circuit, here are some remarkable border destinations to consider.

Kibithu, Arunachal Pradesh

Located in Anjaw district near the India-China border, Kibithu is surrounded by mountains, forests and the Lohit River. Its remote setting makes it ideal for travellers seeking an offbeat Himalayan experience. Visitors can explore suspension bridges, mountain viewpoints and the scenic valleys around the village. However, given its sensitive border location, travellers should check current permit and access requirements before planning a visit.

Delhi Budget: A 5-7 day trip can cost approximately Rs18,000-Rs30,000 per person, including flights or trains, local transport, accommodation and food. Budget stays and homestays can cost around Rs1,000-Rs2,500 per night.

Longwa, Nagaland

Longwa is one of India’s most unusual border villages, situated along the India-Myanmar frontier. The international boundary passes through the village, while the Konyak community preserves a distinctive cultural heritage. Travellers can explore traditional homes, meet local residents and shop for handmade jewellery and wooden crafts. Local customs should be respected, particularly when visiting community spaces.

Delhi Budget: Keep around Rs20,000-Rs35,000 per person for a 4-6 day trip. Homestays generally offer a more affordable option, while food and local transport can add Rs500-Rs1,000 per day.

Dawki, Meghalaya

Dawki, close to the Bangladesh border, is best known for the crystal-clear waters of the Umngot River. Surrounded by the Jaintia Hills, the town is particularly popular with nature lovers and photographers. A boat ride on the Umngot and a visit to the historic Dawki suspension bridge are among the major attractions.

Delhi Budget: A 4-5 day trip can cost roughly Rs12,000-Rs22,000 per person, depending on whether you travel by flight or train. Budget accommodation may range from Rs1,000-Rs2,500 per night, while boating and local sightseeing require an additional budget.

ALSO READ | Budget Traveller | Udaipur Turns Into A Monsoon Paradise: Check Out A 7-Day Tour Plan And Budget

Turtuk, Ladakh

Turtuk is a picturesque village near the India-Pakistan border and offers a distinct introduction to Balti culture. Apricot orchards, traditional houses and dramatic mountain scenery give the village a character different from Leh and other popular Ladakh destinations. Visitors can walk through the village, interact with local families and explore traditional structures and water mills.

Delhi Budget: A 5-7 day Ladakh trip including Turtuk can cost around Rs20,000-Rs35,000 per person on a budget. Homestays may start at approximately Rs1,000-Rs2,500 per night, while local taxi costs can significantly increase the overall expense.

Mana, Uttarakhand

Located close to Badrinath, Mana is popularly promoted as India’s First Village. The high-altitude settlement combines Himalayan scenery with mythology associated with the Mahabharata. Vyas Gufa and Bhim Pul are among the attractions travellers can explore around the village.

Delhi Budget: A 3-4 day trip can cost approximately Rs7,000-Rs12,000 per person by road, including transport, food and budget accommodation. Rooms and homestays can generally cost around Rs800-Rs2,000 per night, depending on the season.

Gunji, Uttarakhand

Located in the Vyas Valley near the India-Nepal-China tri-junction, Gunji is a remote Himalayan settlement associated with routes towards Adi Kailash and Om Parvat. The journey itself is part of the experience, with spectacular mountain landscapes and opportunities to experience the culture of the local Shauka community.

Delhi Budget: A trip can cost around Rs15,000-Rs25,000 per person, depending on the route, permits, transport and duration. Homestays are generally the most practical accommodation option.

Chitkul, Himachal Pradesh

Chitkul, situated along the Baspa River in Kinnaur, is known for its wooden houses, mountain scenery and traditional Himalayan atmosphere. It is often described as the last inhabited village on the old Indo-Tibet trade route. Visitors can explore village lanes, traditional temples and nearby viewpoints while enjoying the surrounding Himalayan landscape.

Delhi Budget: A 4-5 day road trip can cost around Rs8,000-Rs15,000 per person when travelling on a budget. Accommodation can range from Rs800-Rs2,500 per night, while shared taxis and buses can help reduce transport costs.

ALSO READ | Budget Traveller | Explore These 5 Offbeat Weekend Getaways For Under Rs 20,000

Attari, Punjab

Located close to the India-Pakistan border, Attari is famous for the Wagah-Attari border ceremony. The daily Beating Retreat ceremony attracts visitors eager to witness the highly energetic border tradition. A visit can easily be combined with a trip to Amritsar and the Golden Temple.

Delhi Budget: A 2-3 day trip from Delhi can cost around Rs5,000-Rs10,000 per person, including train or bus travel, budget accommodation and local sightseeing. Budget rooms can cost approximately Rs800-Rs2,000 per night.

Dhordo, Gujarat

Located near the Great Rann of Kutch, Dhordo has become a major cultural tourism destination. The village is particularly popular during the Rann Utsav, when the region hosts folk performances, handicraft exhibitions and cultural programmes. Travellers can stay in traditional bhungas, explore Kutchi handicrafts and experience the spectacular white salt desert.

Delhi Budget: A 3-5 day trip can cost around Rs12,000-Rs25,000 per person, depending on transport and the season. Accommodation prices can rise sharply during Rann Utsav, so advance booking is advisable.

Lakhpat, Gujarat

Lakhpat is a historic fortified settlement near the Kori Creek that once prospered as a trading centre. Today, its massive fort walls and historic religious sites offer a fascinating glimpse into the region’s past. The Lakhpat Gurudwara Sahib is an important attraction and is associated with Guru Nanak’s travels.

Delhi Budget: A 3-4 day Gujarat trip covering Lakhpat can cost approximately Rs10,000-Rs20,000 per person, depending on the route and accommodation. Budget stays in nearby towns can cost around Rs800-Rs2,000 per night.

Why Visit India’s Border Villages?

India’s border villages are not simply destinations at the edge of the map. They bring together landscapes, communities, history and traditions that reveal the incredible diversity of the country. From the Himalayan heights of Kibithu and Turtuk to the salt desert of Dhordo and the historic landscape of Attari, each destination offers a different story. Travellers should, however, check current weather conditions, road access and permit requirements before visiting sensitive border regions.

articles.title: Pet First | 5 Dangerous Foods For Dogs That Can Harm Them
articles.description:
Dogs are much more than pets for many families. They are companions who bring affection, energy and plenty of happy moments into our homes. Sharing treats can be one way of showing them love, but not every food that is safe for humans is suitable for dogs. Some common kitchen staples can be toxic to dogs and may cause serious health problems. Knowing which foods to avoid is an important part of responsible pet care.

Chocolate

Chocolate may be a favourite treat for people, but it can be dangerous for dogs because it contains theobromine and caffeine. Depending on the type and amount consumed, chocolate can cause vomiting, diarrhoea, restlessness, abnormal heart rhythms and other serious symptoms. Dark chocolate and cocoa-rich products can be particularly risky. Keep chocolate and chocolate-based desserts safely away from your dog.

ALSO READ | Pet First | 6 Simple Tips To Create Perfect Napping Space For Your Cat

Grapes And Raisins

Grapes and raisins may look like harmless snacks, but they can be dangerous for dogs. Their consumption has been associated with acute kidney injury, and the amount that can cause problems is unpredictable. For this reason, it is safest not to give dogs grapes, raisins or foods containing them. If your dog accidentally eats them, contact a veterinarian promptly.

Onions And Garlic

Onions and garlic belong to the allium family and can damage dogs’ red blood cells, potentially leading to anaemia. The risk applies to different forms, including raw, cooked, dried and powdered versions. Since onion and garlic can be present in gravies, sauces, seasoning mixes and processed foods, check ingredients carefully before sharing human food with your pet.

Macadamia Nuts

Not all nuts are equally dangerous, but macadamia nuts are toxic to dogs and should be avoided. Consumption can result in symptoms such as weakness, vomiting, tremors and difficulty walking. It is best to keep macadamia nuts and foods containing them out of your dog’s reach.

Xylitol

Xylitol is an artificial sweetener found in some sugar-free products, including certain chewing gums, candies and other foods. It can be extremely dangerous to dogs, potentially causing a rapid drop in blood sugar and, in severe cases, liver problems. Always check the ingredient list of sugar-free products before allowing your dog near them. Never assume that a product labelled "sugar-free" is safe for pets.

What To Do If Your Dog Eats A Toxic Food

If your dog accidentally consumes any potentially toxic food, contact a veterinarian or emergency veterinary service immediately. Do not wait for symptoms to appear, as some poisoning cases can become serious quickly. Keep the food packaging or ingredient information available when speaking to the veterinarian. This can help them assess what your dog consumed.

ALSO READ | Pet First | 6 Essential Things To Know Before Bringing Fur Baby Home

Choose Dog-Safe Treats

Giving your dog treats is a wonderful way to show affection, but the safest option is to choose foods specifically suitable for dogs. Avoid sharing leftovers or processed snacks unless you know the ingredients are safe. A little caution can go a long way. Keeping toxic foods securely stored and educating everyone in the household about what dogs should not eat can help prevent accidental poisoning and keep your four-legged companion healthy.
